source.title: A Guardrail for Safety Preservation: When Safety-Sensitive Subspace Meets Harmful-Resistant Null-Space
source.authors: Bing-Jie Zhang; Yi-Bo Yang; Zhen-Jiang Ren; Dan-Dan Guo; Jindong Gu; P. Torr; Bernard Ghanem

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It reports harmful-output scores after fine-tuning on clean and unsafe mixtures, and tests a different, subspace-based approach to safety localization than the claim’s original studies.
record.gate_note: The paper measures harmfulness score (HS), the proportion of outputs flagged unsafe by a moderation classifier; it does not directly report refusal rates. Its training-data ratio experiments and subspace-removal analysis bear on V1, V2 and V5. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant-prefix effects, or safety deepening. Results merely cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a defence-method paper, but its plain-LoRA baselines report harmfulness rates of safety-tuned chat models after fine-tuning. One is clean (p=0) and others have 50–200 harmful examples mixed into 1,000-example task sets. These measured rates bear on V1 and V2. The judge (beaver-dam moderation classifier) and data recipe differ from the originals, so this is a different method on the same question. The subspace and SVD-truncation results do not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that GuardSpace, combining safety-irrelevant-subspace adapter initialization with a harmful-input null-space projector, keeps HS near base level while matching or improving task accuracy. It sustains low HS with up to 20% unsafe data. The projector is the main safety driver, and the initialization gives smaller gains. The conclusion lists Llama-3-8B-Instruct among the models, but the experiments report Qwen-2-7B-Instruct, so that line is inconsistent with the results.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes covariance-preconditioned weight decomposition for adapter initialization and a harmful-input null-space projector during fine-tuning; this is not the original studies’ measurement or intervention recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with unsafe-data ratio, model, task dataset, harmful-prompt corpus and size, adapter rank, and whether the null-space projector is used.

fits_no_version.finding: Discarding up to 1,024 smallest covariance-preconditioned (activation-aware) SVD components keeps ASR at 1.82–5.15%. Plain SVD truncation makes ASR spike, and in Fig. 4 initializing adapters from 1,024 components causes an HS spike.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal survives activation-aware low-rank truncation of weights, but not activation-agnostic truncation. Which weight components matter for safety depends on the decomposition used.

record.problems: HS is a moderation-classifier score, not a direct refusal rate. No uncertainty estimates are stated. The paper’s description of the prompt set for Figure 3a differs from the figure’s HEx-PHI axis label. The conclusion names Llama-3-8B-Instruct, whereas the main model results report Qwen-2-7B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-IT.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the 60-row cap. Comparative defensive-method results not needed to record the tested LoRA fine-tuning effects or the subspace-localization results are not included.

untested.parts: Full-parameter fine-tuning; purely harmful training sets; fewer than 50 harmful examples; near-total compliance; any model beyond the three 7–9B chat models with rank-8 q/v LoRA.
Benign datasets other than GSM8K; models other than Llama-2-7B-Chat; carefully selected benign data; full fine-tuning.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models; not measured.
Prefilling, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes; not measured.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety; the truncation sweep removes non-safety components and does not isolate safety-carrying ones.
Deepening safety beyond the first tokens; not studied.

record.verdict_notes: Only the plain-LoRA baseline cells bear on the claim; the defence comparisons do not. HS comes from the beaver-dam-7b moderation classifier, not refusal rate or a GPT-4 judge, and is single-run with no uncertainty. Harmful data are mixed with task data (1000p unsafe), so V1 here concerns poisoned mixtures rather than pure harmful sets. Figure 3a's text cites AdvBench via Yuan et al. 2023b, which is ASVD, while the axis reads HEx-PHI. Table 4's 'w/o null space projector' (HS 52.00) and Fig. 3b's no-projector ASR (>20% after 6–7 epochs) use the study's own initialization, not plain LoRA, so they are not claim rows.

versions.untested_parts: The study varies unsafe-data proportions up to 0.20 in 1,000-example training sets, but does not test the full range of few to a few hundred examples or whether refusal is removed almost entirely.
Tests clean GSM8K fine-tuning; does not test a range of ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction datasets.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
Compliant-prefix prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
Does not establish that safety generally resides in a small number of parameters or ranks; it evaluates its own covariance-preconditioned decomposition and adapter initialization.
Whether training data or the training objective causes first-token shallowness.
Training safety beyond the first response tokens and testing whether such deepening holds up.

rows.note: The text reports a range across the rank sweep rather than separate values for each rank. The accompanying figure's axis label and text's stated prompt set do not match.
rows.check: This measures whether discarding the smallest covariance-preconditioned components keeps ASR low. That is the complement of localization: it shows low-ranked parts can be removed, not that a small set carries safety. There is no utility check, so safety is not separated from general capability. Prompt set is inconsistent (text: AdvBench; axis: HEx-PHI). Belongs under fits_no_version.

relationships.condition: AGNEWS task, Qwen-2-7B-Instruct, and the p=0.15 setting
relationships.reason: Rises are much weaker: AGNEWS 17.6 vs 2.4 (r2), Qwen 30.0 vs 4.8 (r8). HS dips to 34.0 at p=0.15 (r6), so the effect depends on task, model and run, and stays far from near-total compliance.
relationships.display_finding: Harmful score rose much less, to 17.6 against 2.4 on AGNEWS and 30.0 against 4.8 on Qwen, and dipped to 34.0 at p=0.15, so the effect depends on task, model and run and stays far from near-total compliance.
